findings.title: Three test lines exceed the 88-character limit and will fail CI (`ruff check` E501 and `ruff format --check`)
findings.description:
`pyproject.toml` sets `line-length = 88` with `select = ["E", ...]` and no per-file ignore, and CI runs `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`. Three lines in the new test files exceed 88 characters because a trailing `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` comment was appended instead of wrapping the call:

- `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:140` (~138 chars): `sequence = SignalSequence(UNIT_RANGE, (_event(100, confidence=0.0), _event(200, confidence=1)))  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`
- `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:85` (~113 chars): `({"time": Timestamp(1.5, TimeMeaning.AVAILABLE_AT)}, r"time\.ns"),  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`
- `tests/core_model/test_labels.py:66` (~109 chars): `vocabulary = LabelVocabulary("regime.trend", {0, 1, 2}, UNIT_RANGE)  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`

Each will be flagged by E501 and is not in canonical `ruff format` shape, so both CI lint steps fail on this commit. Fix: wrap the argument lists (the `pyright: ignore` comment then lands on the closing line, where the suppressed call expression still spans). All `pyright: ignore` comments I verified against the code are genuinely needed in strict mode (e.g. `test_labels.py:107` for a `set[int]` literal, `test_signals.py:74` for `confidence: 1`), so only the three long lines need reformatting, not the suppressions.

findings.title: "Element loop" guard is now defined twice with different semantics, and the comment in test_confidence.py doesn't match its file
findings.description:
The established project guard in `tests/core_model/test_import_boundary.py` counts `ast.GeneratorExp` as an element loop and even self-tests that (`test_loop_guard_detects_every_loop_form` includes `"z = sum(x for x in y)\n"`). The new `test_confidence.py` and `test_labels.py` each redefine a local `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` tuple that excludes `ast.GeneratorExp`, with the comment "A generator expression is allowed: `all(...)` over one is not an array pass." Consequences:

1. The new modules do rely on that exemption — `labels.py` uses `all(... for category in self.category_ids)` and `np.fromiter((event.time.ns for event in events))`-style generators — so a guard that silently permits element-wide generator loops is a weaker check than the project's own standard for the same invariant ("every check is one NumPy expression").
2. The exemption comment was copied verbatim into `test_confidence.py`, where `confidence.py` contains no `all(...)` and no generator expression at all, so the justification describes code that isn't there.
3. The AST-scan logic is now triplicated (`test_import_boundary.py`, `test_confidence.py`, `test_labels.py`).

Suggested resolution: centralize one loop-detection helper (and one decision about whether generator expressions count) — e.g. in `tests/core_model/conftest.py` — and reuse it from all three test files, fixing the stale comment while at it. Not blocking: the for/while/comprehension forms are still caught everywhere.

findings.title: `require_optional_range` parameter order is inconsistent with the sibling validators
findings.description: Every other validator in `validation.py`/`value_checks.py` takes `(value, field, error)` — `require_instance(value, expected, field, error)`, `require_name(value, field, error)`, `require_real(value, field, error)`, `require_dotted_id(value, field, error)` — but `require_optional_range(value, error, field="confidence_range")` puts `error` second. All four call sites (`confidence.py`, `labels.py`, `signals.py`, `declarations.py`) pass `error` positionally, so a caller coming from the other helpers could plausibly pass a field name where the error class is expected. Consider `(value, field, error)` matching the house style, or making `field` keyword-only with a clear name.
